Subject: FinLedger connectivity ops check-in: PrivateLink vs peering & egress IPs

Hi Amit / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion on the production timeline and security bar. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can lock down the deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and get networking prepped for the POC.

Summary of what we heard:
- You want all traffic for the POC to stay within your AWS environment; preference for PrivateLink but open to peering if there are constraints.
- Security team needs static egress IPs for outbound connections and evidence for SOC2 controls.
- Target POC date window: week of May 17 — procurement and network prep need to be completed before then.

Action items / questions for your network/security folks:
1) Which AWS account and VPC ID will we connect to (account number + VPC CIDR)?
2) Do you have a Transit Gateway in front of your VPCs, or will we be connecting directly to a single VPC?
3) Preference: PrivateLink (Redwood exposes an endpoint service in our account) OR VPC Peering? Any strong blockers for PrivateLink from your side?
4) Are you able to accept the standard outbound ports (HTTPS 443) only, or do you need additional ports (we sometimes need SSH 22 for managed troubleshooting but can arrange ephemeral access)?
5) Confirm the egress allowlist process — do you need a fixed list of IPs from us, or will we publish a short-lived CIDR and rotate?
6) Please loop in procurement contact and SOC/security contact (we need to send a short questionnaire and the PrivateLink spec).

I attached a one-line CSV template for the networking details to make it easy to fill in. Karthik will follow up with the PrivateLink connection spec and the minimal routing rules we require.

Thanks — if you can reply inline with answers to the numbered items that’ll be perfect.

—Logan

Logan — thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline below.

1) AWS account: 123456789012. Primary VPC for the POC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (10.10.0.0/16).
2) We have a Transit Gateway in our prod stack but for the POC we'd likely connect to a single VPC first.
3) Preference is PrivateLink — security prefers endpoint services over peering when feasible, because it limits route exposure. No hard blockers but we need the PrivateLink architecture doc for approval.
4) HTTPS 443 is sufficient for normal traffic. For any managed troubleshooting we can grant temporary SSH via a bastion with a short-lived ticket.
5) We require a fixed set of egress IP addresses to allowlist in our outbound egress firewall (we don't accept rotating ranges for the POC). You'll need to provide these ASAP.
6) Procurement: Priya Sinha (cc'd). Security: security@finledger.com (cc'd).

Also attaching a short network inventory CSV filled with the fields you requested. We'll aim to get procurement sign-off by May 5.

- Amit

Subject: Re: FinLedger connectivity ops check-in: PrivateLink vs peering & egress IPs

Hi Amit — thanks for the fast turnaround and for filling the CSV. A few technical clarifications and what we'll provide on our side: 

A. PrivateLink (recommended path)
- We will provision an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) in our account and expose a PrivateLink endpoint service. FinLedger will create an interface endpoint in account 123456789012 and attach to your subnet.
- Required inputs from you: VPC ID, list of subnets (private subnets for endpoint ENIs), and the security groups for the endpoint ENIs.
- Egress IPs: for requests we make back to your systems (webhooks/health checks) we can provide a static set of NAT egress IPs. For the POC we can commit to the following public IPs (these are our provisioning IPs; final ranges will be in the PrivateLink spec): 34.203.12.45, 34.203.12.46, 34.203.12.47. Please confirm these can be allowlisted — if you need a CIDR we can provide a /29.

B. VPC Peering (alternate)
- If you prefer peering, note: peering does not support cross-account PrivateLink-style controlled endpoints; you would need to manage route table propagation and our egress might come from different NATs. Peering can work but will require changes to your route tables and possibly TGW configuration.

C. Minimal security requirements
- TLS terminated at our NLB (we can use ACM certs).
- Health-check path: /_health (443).
- Port: 443 only (unless you request SSH for troubleshooting).

D. SOC2 & audit evidence
- We'll send a short pack with our SOC2 report extract and the PrivateLink spec. For security review, expect a one-business-day turnaround from our compliance team once we receive the questionnaire.

I've attached the PrivateLink spec PDF which contains the schema for the endpoint creation, the sample AWS CLI commands, and the allowlist IPs described above. Final IP list will be replicated in the production readiness packet.

Next steps I propose:
- FinLedger to confirm allowlist for the three public IPs above (or request a /29).
- Provide the subnet(s) to host the interface endpoint and the AWS role we should use for cross-account acceptance (we will provide the service name).
- Procurement to confirm PO timeline (we heard May 5).

If you confirm the IP allowlist and subnets by EOD April 22 we can schedule endpoint creation and acceptance the week of May 3.

—Karthik
